To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a climate club can reduce global emissions effectively, even if it is initiated by only a few countries, provided it offers sufficiently large incentives to reluctant countries, is reasonably unconstrained by conflict between its members over issues beyond the climate, and is initiated by the United State and European Union.

1) the club approach is an effective and promising alternative to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change; 2) it is more promising than the Kyoto Protocol; 3) a climate club can emerge and grow even when the club is small and the members are not all enthusiastic; and 4) the club approach can work with a wide variety of club designs, including a club with conditional commitments.

a climate club can reduce global emissions effectively and can persist and grow if it is initiated by the ‘Right’ constellation of actors and offers sufficiently large incentives for hesitant countries and is reasonably unconstrained by internal conflicts.
